title: Who Names Living Things? Explained Simply | PUC Biology Class 11
description:
Diya sorts her kitchen spice box in one minute, then looks out at the garden: millions of kinds of living things, and every one needs a place and a name. Who sorts all of this?

You will see the four basic processes of taxonomy (characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature) and what taxonomists look at. A China rose from the garden is characterised part by part with labelled diagrams of the plant, the flower and the leaf, then identified, placed in a group and named Hibiscus rosa-sinensis. We see why identification must come before naming, where the word systematics comes from (systema, Linnaeus and Systema Naturae, 1735) and what it adds: evolutionary relationships. Then a side by side comparison, a pause and think check, why taxonomy matters, a worked example, the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions.

This is Episode 5 of our PUC Biology series.
Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and NEET students.
